column3: “In the hand of” is rendered “under the command of.”
“Set heart to us” is rendered “care about us.” The Hebrew reads “now like us ten thousand”; NASB renders “you are worth ten thousand of us,” as in some manuscripts.
“To gentleness for me” is rendered “Deal gently for my sake.”
“Was met” is rendered “happened to meet,” and “was put between heaven and earth” as “was left hanging.”
“And on me to give” is rendered “I would have given,” and “ten silver” as “ten pieces of silver.”
The Hebrew reads “protect, whoever, the young man”; NASB renders “Protect for me,” as in some manuscripts.
The Hebrew written text reads “on my life”; NASB renders “against his life,” following the reading tradition. NASB adds parentheses.
“I will not wait thus before you” is rendered “I will not waste time here with you.” “Spears” translates a word that may mean “sticks.”
“Good news finding” is rendered “no reward for going.”
“Peace” is rendered “All is well,” and “bowed down” as “prostrated himself.”
NASB rearranges the difficult Hebrew (“to send the king’s servant Joab and your servant”).
